protocol: B-52 flight. Hatch loss at 4,000 ft aircraft altitude and ascent to 15,000 ft. The body describes cabin pressure altitude held at 8,000 ft except for 30 seconds at 10,000 ft. Cabin altitude at symptom onset is not specified.
outcome_window: Joint pain began suddenly after decompression and persisted through landing. Complete pain relief occurred during recompression. Post-treatment observation duration was not given.
note: Case Report calls the diagnosis presumptive and Discussion questions its specificity. The abstract says there was no diving history, while the case narrative reports a shallow dive ten days earlier. The event date and overlap with broader USAF aggregate treatment archives are unverified.

protocol: Naval student pilot flying an unpressurized aircraft at 14,000 ft. The paper describes recurrent right-knee discomfort on prior flights and prior injury with a retained screw. The patient denied diving.
outcome_window: Pain began after about 40 minutes at altitude, persisted two hours after flight and was unchanged on the Monday visit. The author reports essential relief after 20 minutes under the reported conditions and complete relief after one hour of recompression. Formal follow-up duration was not given.
note: Selected flight with probable bends as judged by the author. The initial clinic diagnosis was patellofemoral pain. No exposure denominator was enumerated.

protocol: Unpressurized cargo aircraft. Climb to flight level 290 took 26 minutes. Both pilots reportedly used oxygen masks. The copilot became symptomatic shortly after leveling; the pilot in command was reported unaffected during the incident.
outcome_window: Initial skin symptoms about ten minutes after leveling at flight level 290. Consciousness returned shortly after descent to flight level 100. The abstract reports pulmonary edema and collapse eight hours after landing. The case narrative gives eight hours asleep before symptoms on waking. Hospital discharge was on source day 5.
locator: Case Report, abstract and Fig. 2, pp. 990–992
note: The authors describe severe DCS, with subsequent shock and pulmonary edema. No hyperbaric treatment was performed. Clinical and exposure denominators outside this selected report are unavailable.
